card.name: Inside 'stimulating' and 'incited' words
card.fires_on: Partway through the word 'stimulating' or 'incited', just before the rest of it is spelled out. Mostly in 'follicle-stimulating hormone' and 'colony-stimulating factor'.

modes.label: Follicle-stimulating hormone
modes.description: The last piece of 'follicle' before 'stimulating hormone (FSH)' in lab test lists.
modes.example: 5.19 Laboratory Tests Serum follic<<le>> stimulating hormone (FSH) and estr

modes.label: Colony-stimulating factor
modes.description: The hyphen piece or the start of 'stimulating' after 'colony' in 'colony-stimulating factors'.
modes.example: Cell counts usually begin to recover within 3 to 7 days after discontinuing drug. Colony<<-st>>imulating factors have been shown to increase

modes.label: Incited
modes.description: The 'inc' piece of 'incited' in a history passage.
modes.example: Constantius condoned and even<< inc>>ited the persecution of Athanasius.

card.writes: It pushes toward words meaning encourage, stimulate or incite, in English and Chinese.
card.plain: It fires when a word like 'stimulating' or 'incited' is only partly written, and it expects the meaning of encouraging or stimulating.
